players.product: submarine and underground power-cable installation and maintenance (also subsea telecom-cable laying)

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report: H1 2026 consolidated revenue rose 33% year on year to KRW 148.2 billion - subsea cable construction and maintenance KRW 42.8 billion, underground cable construction (subsidiary LS BuildWin) KRW 105.4 billion; domestic KRW 11.9 billion, overseas KRW 136.3 billion. Q2 2026 revenue KRW 95,440,344 thousand (Q2 2025: KRW 66,986,960 thousand). H1 operating profit KRW 10,337 million (subsea KRW 6,919 million, underground KRW 3,418 million), up from KRW 6,435,720,790 in H1 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue KRW 148,235 million (+33% YoY); Q2 revenue KRW 95,440,344 thousand vs KRW 66,986,960 thousand; H1 operating profit KRW 10,337 million

quarterly_data.signal: Order backlog at end-H1 2026 of KRW 664.6 billion: subsea cable KRW 63.6 billion, underground cable KRW 601.0 billion (cumulative orders KRW 1,030.9 billion, delivered KRW 366.3 billion). Remaining performance obligations are scheduled at KRW 382,671,284 thousand for 2026, KRW 231,774,517 thousand for 2027 and KRW 50,152,782 thousand for 2028 and later.
quarterly_data.figure: Order backlog KRW 664.6 billion (subsea KRW 63.6 billion, underground KRW 601.0 billion); RPO KRW 664,598,583 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Installation fleet: payload of the cable-laying barge GL2030 being raised from 4,000 t to about 7,000 t for larger offshore wind projects (KRW 19,830 million conversion approved 03-25-2025; the history lists the capacity expansion completed in 2026.06). A new 13,000-ton-class cable-laying vessel (CLV) was ordered from the Tersan shipyard (Turkey) on 06-28-2025 for KRW 345.8 billion, delivery expected in Q2 2028; the company says the GL2030 barge cannot serve the European market and is limited in long-distance, high-capacity Asian lays, which the CLV is meant to overcome. The filing states the company plans to operate four cable-laying vessels in total by H1 2028, including the one under construction.
quarterly_data.figure: New CLV 13,000 t payload, KRW 345,800,000 thousand; GL2030 payload to about 7,000 t (KRW 19,830,000 thousand conversion)

quarterly_data.signal: Offshore wind support business: in a consortium with Taiwanese vessel operator DFO the company is bidding to supply a service operation vessel (SOV) to turbine maker Vestas for a domestic offshore wind project; it was selected preferred bidder in Q2 2025 and expects to sign the contract within 2026. It also plans SOV bids for the Taean and Anma offshore wind projects, is building a subsea power-cable maintenance (IMR) business with LS Cable & System, and is developing an offshore wind installation port with Haenam County. Revenue from offshore wind development/operation is expected after 2028.

Parent LS Cable & System is the main customer: related-party sales to LS Cable & System were KRW 113,239,243 thousand in H1 2026 (H1 2025: KRW 71,880,789 thousand); the underground segment wins orders jointly with LS Cable & System. Open contracts include LS Cable & System Singapore 230kV underground projects NDC 409 (KRW 128,320 million, 2.9% complete), NDC 355 (KRW 126,840 million), NDC 343 (KRW 126,769 million), NDC 376 (KRW 87,186 million) and NDC 403 (KRW 43,627 million, signed 12-10-2025).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 sales to LS Cable & System KRW 113,239,243 thousand (H1 2025 KRW 71,880,789 thousand)

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center grid work: subsidiary LS BuildWin is building the 154kV underground transmission line for the Ansan data center (client Ansan Green Energy PFV); contract KRW 9,720 million signed 08-01-2023, 62.2% complete at end-H1 2026, completion deadline 04-10-2028.

Other projects: JAKO submarine optical-cable installation KRW 36,897 million (06-20-2025 to 08-11-2027, 21.6% complete); TPC Offshore Wind Power Generation Phase 2 (Taiwan) submarine cable trenching and burial, contract KRW 17,515 million; Taean offshore wind EWA contract signed 02-13-2026 (due 06-30-2027); Yokohama Zone submarine telecom-cable maintenance agreement produced H1 2026 maintenance revenue of KRW 13,531,468 thousand. The Anma offshore wind project contract was terminated on 04-24-2026, leaving KRW 3,715,574 thousand of capitalised contract-fulfilment cost whose recovery awaits settlement.
quarterly_data.figure: JAKO KRW 36,897 million; TPC Phase 2 KRW 17,515 million; maintenance revenue KRW 13,531,468 thousand; Anma cost KRW 3,715,574 thousand
